Worley EPC mechanical specialties rarely transfer between each other.
blockers.fix: Major pulls the full requirement detail from the Airswift VMS portal to identify the mechanical specialty and any required design tools before sourcing.

blockers.detail: Both bill rate and pay rate are blank, so there's no number to back into a target pay or to qualify a principal-level contractor against in the Denver market.

reqs.role_summary: A contract Principal-level Mechanical Engineer seat at Worley's Denver office, sourced through the Airswift VMS — almost certainly EPC project engineering (fixed/rotating equipment, pressure vessels, or piping mechanical) but the actual specialty isn't stated.

reqs.peer_coaching_note: Major — a bare title, location, and contract terms isn't enough to source a Worley EPC principal; pull the VMS req detail for the mechanical specialty and the posted bill rate before this goes to a recruiter, since both are blank right now.

actions.action: Pull the full requirement write-up from the Airswift VMS portal to nail down the mechanical specialty (fixed equipment/vessels vs. rotating vs. piping) and any required design software before any sourcing starts.
actions.why_it_matters: Without the specialty the recruiter sources the wrong pool — EPC mechanical disciplines don't cross over and a wrong-discipline submittal gets bounced.

The only friction is geographic narrowing per the 12/2 note and the typical scarcity of PE-level bridge engineers willing to relocate to these markets.
reqs.role_summary: This is a licensed (or near-licensed) bridge/transportation civil engineer with PM responsibilities — designing DOT/turnpike/county/municipal bridge projects and managing them from scoping to final plans at a regional A&E firm.
reqs.realistic_candidate_profile: A 5-15 YOE bridge engineer with a Kansas (or readily reciprocal) PE who's done DOT/KDOT/turnpike bridge design in Civil 3D or MicroStation/OpenRoads plus the bridge analysis stack (LEAP, OpenBridge, LARSA, BRASS). At $80-125K W2 direct-hire onsite in Wichita/KC/OKC, this is a Midwest A&E professional who values longevity — not a job-hopper or remote seeker.
reqs.peer_coaching_note: Zoie — your 12/2 Kansas-focus note never made it into the body, so the pod is still working the original OKC/three-office spread; push that update and pin down whether this is the PE/PM tier or a mid-level designer so the $80-125K band actually means something.

actions.action: Update the working location target to Wichita-primary / KS-preferred per your own 12/2 note, and tell Brooke's pod OKC is exceptional-candidates-only so they stop sourcing OKC broadly.
actions.why_it_matters: The body still says OKC/three-office spread; without aligning the recruiter to the 12/2 note, submittals will keep coming in for the wrong geography (already 3 submittals deep at 322 days open).

actions.action: Confirm with the VMS/client contact whether this opening is the senior PM/PE tier (top of band) or a mid-level designer, and document a bill rate or confirm the direct-hire fee structure.
actions.why_it_matters: Both bill and pay rate failed the critical gate; on a $45K-wide direct-hire band the recruiter needs to know which tier to target and what the placement economics are.

actions.action: Clarify whether PE licensure is a true gate for this specific seat or genuinely flexible, given the role is the main client point of contact.
actions.why_it_matters: If PE is effectively required, sourcing unlicensed candidates wastes cycles; if truly flexible, the pool widens materially in these markets.

actions.action: Note the no-sponsorship and W2-only constraints in the screen so candidates requiring sponsorship are filtered up front.
actions.why_it_matters: MKEC explicitly offers no sponsorship; screening late costs submittals.

Minor friction comes from the YOE conflict between the client comment (5-10 yrs) and the formal requirement (3+ yrs), plus the W2-only/no-sponsorship gate.
reqs.role_summary: A direct-hire land development civil engineer for MKEC's OKC office — designs site/grading/paving/water/wastewater/drainage for residential, commercial, and municipal projects under a PM. This is a mid-level consulting civil engineer role, not an O&G role.

At $80-125K direct hire onsite, this is a realistic and competitive offer for the OKC market; the pool is local civil consultants at firms like Olsson, Garver, Halff, or Johnson & Associates.
reqs.peer_coaching_note: Zoie — this one's workable as-is, just reconcile the 5-10 vs 3+ YOE split and pin the real salary target by tier so Brooke's pod isn't submitting against a moving target after 322 days open.

actions.action: Confirm the budgeted salary target by experience tier (e.g., what a non-PE 4-yr vs a PE 7-yr lands) so the $80-125K band maps to real offers.

reqs.title: Senior Substation Electrical Engineer
reqs.recruitability_rationale: The role, skills, software stack, YOE bands, location/remote signal, and the disqualifiers are all spelled out in unusual detail — a recruiter knows exactly who to search for and who to exclude. Both rates are TBD but the client explicitly wants candidate-requested rates (so the recruiter works to candidate ask), which removes the rate gap as a sourcing blocker; minor friction comes from CC/VMS access limits and the broad Senior-through-Sr-Principal span in one req.
reqs.role_summary: Senior/Principal substation physical design engineer doing greenfield and brownfield HV switchyard/substation design (69kV+) for Worley's Power Networks group — detailed deliverables (layouts, grounding, transformer sizing, studies) plus lead/mentoring on a temp-to-perm W2 basis, mostly remote on East Coast time.
reqs.realistic_candidate_profile: A substation physical design engineer with 8-12+ years at an EPC or power-delivery firm (Burns & McDonnell, POWER Engineers, Sargent & Lundy, Quanta, Black & Veatch) who has personally produced HV substation deliverables and run studies in ETAP/SKM/EasyPower/CDEGS. They'll be remote-friendly US-based, PE strongly preferred for the Principal tier, and they want a contract rate that pencils to a sensible perm salary — utility-only candidates without detailed design production won't qualify.
reqs.peer_coaching_note: Major — this is actually a well-detailed client spec; the only things to tighten are splitting the Senior-vs-Principal pools and locking the contract-and-perm rate on every screen so your submittals stop stalling.

actions.action: Confirm with Vicki/iCIMS rep whether this single req should be split or prioritized Senior vs Principal first, since the screening questions span 7-20 years across two distinct levels.
actions.why_it_matters: Without a priority tier the recruiter spreads submittals across two pools and risks the 4-submittal-in-93-days drift continuing.

actions.action: Capture the realistic contract hourly AND post-conversion salary expectation on every screen (per client questions 16/17, salary must not exceed the annualized hourly) so submittals aren't dead on rate.
actions.why_it_matters: Both bill and pay rate are TBD and the client is buying at candidate-requested rates — a submittal with mismatched contract-vs-perm numbers gets rejected.

actions.action: Build a hard screen on the work-authorization rule: TN-visa candidates cannot work remotely and must relocate to Reading PA office; all others remote-from-US OK, California discouraged for time zone.
actions.why_it_matters: Submitting a remote TN candidate wastes a submittal and burns client trust on a 13%-win CC account.

actions.action: Mine prior Worley/Airswift EPC substation contractor history and B&McD/S&L/POWER alumni for fast restarts rather than relying on the VMS pipeline.
actions.why_it_matters: 93 days open with only 4 submittals signals the open-market pull is weak; warm EPC design talent moves the needle faster.

submittal_intel.pipeline_summary: Three real submittals all still in-flight: Jose Cardoza (Client Submission 3/23), Pandu Karanam (Interview Scheduled, last moved 5/12), and Ernesto Cornieles (Client Submission 5/20). reqs.title: Revenue Cycle-Patient Accounting Director
reqs.recruitability_rationale: The role, skills, location, and salary floor are all clearly defined and the candidate pool (Epic Resolute HB/PB revenue cycle leaders) is well-understood and sourceable. Minor friction comes from a salary floor that may be light for a true system director and a rigid 'no-budge' requirements stance that narrows the pool.
reqs.role_summary: A direct-hire healthcare revenue cycle leader running patient financial services (hospital + professional billing, claims, cash posting, AR) for Saint Francis, with deep Epic Resolute HB/PB depth and prior director-level leadership.
reqs.role_family: Healthcare revenue cycle / patient accounting leadership
reqs.realistic_candidate_profile: A current revenue cycle manager or director from a mid-to-large hospital system running Epic Resolute HB/PB, 8+ years in hospital and professional billing, bachelor's degree, already in or willing to relocate to Tulsa. At a ~$100K starting salary this is at the lower end for a system-level director, so the realistic hire skews toward a strong RC manager stepping up or a director from a smaller/similarly-paid market.
reqs.peer_coaching_note: Carley — this one's workable today; the thing to nail down is whether $100K is a floor or a cap, because a system-level Epic Resolute RC director usually runs higher and that single answer decides whether you're sourcing step-up managers or seasoned directors.

actions.action: Confirm with Cynthia/Jackie whether the $100,131.20 is a true ceiling-area starting figure or a floor with room — a system-level RC director with deep Epic Resolute typically commands more, and a hard ~$100K cap will shape who you can realistically land.
actions.why_it_matters: If $100K is firm, the recruiter should target step-up managers and smaller-system directors, not seasoned large-system directors who'll price out — wrong targeting wastes the whole search.

actions.action: Pin down with the VMS/client contact exactly which requirements are the true non-negotiables (Epic Resolute, 8 yrs HB+PB, bachelor's, director-level) versus nice-to-haves, given the 'won't budge on anything listed' note.
actions.why_it_matters: A blanket no-budge stance plus an Epic AI-implementation line can shrink the pool to near-zero; knowing the real gates prevents over-screening.

actions.action: Confirm the OSCN background check expectations and relocation eligibility (71-mile radius / $10K) so candidates outside Tulsa are pre-qualified before submittal.
actions.why_it_matters: OSCN is a hard gate and relocation eligibility affects which out-of-market candidates are even viable; pre-screening avoids late fallout.

reqs.title: Regulatory and Compliance Specialist
reqs.recruitability_rationale: Role, skills, location, and comp are all clear and the pool of Houston O&G regulatory/compliance people is real and reachable — 22 submittals in already proves it's sourceable. The only friction is reconciling the seniority the PHMSA + multi-state ask implies against the stated 3-year floor and the flat $150k, plus pinning the direct-hire fee.
reqs.role_summary: A direct-hire O&G regulatory/compliance specialist for a gas producer (TGNR) who handles state and federal agency filings, permitting, inactive-well compliance, and PHMSA pipeline-safety awareness — a regulatory affairs role, not a field safety role despite the boilerplate physical-demands section.
reqs.realistic_candidate_profile: A Houston-based regulatory/compliance professional with 3-8 years working Texas RRC and Louisiana state filings plus federal PHMSA/DOT/OSHA awareness, typically coming from an upstream or midstream operator's regulatory/EH&S compliance group. At $150k DH this skews toward the senior end of the stated 3-year floor — someone who has actually owned agency relationships and permitting files, not an entry compliance coordinator.
reqs.peer_coaching_note: Jordan — this is sourceable and you've got 22 in, but 67 days with no close smells like a level/comp mismatch; nail down whether $150k buys a 3-year coordinator or a senior regulatory-affairs person and whether PHMSA is really required vs. RRC/state experience.

actions.action: Confirm with Olivia whether $150k is a flat number or the top of a band, and what experience level it's really aimed at (the JD says 3-year floor but PHMSA + multi-state reads more like 5-8 years).
actions.why_it_matters: 22 submittals over 67 days with no close suggests a possible level/comp mismatch — recruiters may be sending the wrong tier of candidate.

actions.action: Clarify whether PHMSA pipeline-regs experience is a true must-have or whether strong TX RRC / Louisiana state regulatory experience is the real target, and relay to the pod.
actions.why_it_matters: Determines whether the pool is narrow pipeline-integrity people or the much larger upstream regulatory-affairs pool.

actions.action: Document the direct-hire placement fee / bill basis on the req so the desk knows the economics.
actions.why_it_matters: Both rate fields are blank on a DH; salary is known but the fee isn't, which is needed before offer stage.

actions.action: Capture non-negotiables and degree enforcement — the JD allows HS diploma + 6 years in lieu of degree, so confirm whether the bachelor's is actually firm.
actions.why_it_matters: If the degree is waivable, experienced no-degree candidates shouldn't be screened out.

reqs.title: Field Service Tech - Columbus
reqs.recruitability_rationale: Clear role, clear skills, clear location, and a documented pay range — fully sourceable today. Minor friction only because the body, client comments, and AM notes carry several stale/conflicting numbers (pay, travel %, YOE, cohort dates) that the recruiter must reconcile to the latest 6/1 note to pitch accurately.
reqs.role_summary: Entry-to-mid field service technician who installs, commissions, and maintains large SCR catalyst/silencer equipment at customer sites, traveling ~75% with home weekends; a hands-on electrical/mechanical aptitude role, not an engineering role.
reqs.role_family: Field service technician — industrial emissions/SCR equipment (electrical/mechanical)
reqs.realistic_candidate_profile: A 1-6 YOE field service / instrumentation / industrial maintenance tech comfortable with AC/DC circuits, relay logic, and basic I&C, who is willing to travel 3 of 4 weeks and pass drug/background. At $27-30+/hr starting in the Midwest, this is a military-tech, trade-school, HVAC/elevator/wind-turbine/generator-service, or recent industrial-electrician profile based out of or willing to relocate near Columbus.
reqs.peer_coaching_note: Carley — this one's recruitable, but the req has three generations of numbers stacked in it (body, client comments, your 6/1 note); drop a single clean summary line at the top so the pod isn't pitching dead June cohorts or the wrong pay tier.

actions.action: Anchor the recruiter to the latest 6/1 AM note as truth: pay is tiered $27-40/hr ($27/hr start for Midwest/Columbus), Level I-II focus (1-6 YOE), and active cohorts are now August 9 and September 13 — the June 14/July 12 dates in the body are past.

actions.action: Confirm with the Miratech contact (Ausra) whether DP Fee 20% / Direct Hire is correct given the W2 hourly framing, and document the placement structure for the recruiter.
actions.why_it_matters: The role reads as direct-hire but is described as W2 hourly with OT and per diem — recruiter and candidate need a clear comp/employment story before submittals.

actions.action: Reconcile the travel figure for the pitch — body says 60-75% overnight, role highlights say 75% (3 of 4 weeks), client comments say 3-of-4 with paid travel time; lock one number candidates can plan their lives around.
actions.why_it_matters: Travel load is the #1 fallout driver on this role; an inconsistent pitch produces accepts that wash out in week one.
